title: SO-1.08 Decision queue: blockers and user decisions as one workflow with named states
request: Closes G-SO-08 (addendum 8, review row 8). Source: the Scope One addendum (PR #222, docs/scope-one/ADDENDUM-ARCHITECTURE-AND-DELIVERY-REVIEW.md at head a1757a0) and its review table (issuecomment-6534383323); owner request of 31 Oct 2026 that every aspect be decomposed in the WBS and built into contracts (t531u). The addendum names recommendations that become contracts on acceptance; this contract is the design-record stage, so it asks for the decision record and builds nothing. Contracts marked with a dagger are signed in the owner's vault and are not visible in this repository. Depends on contracts: SO-03-A, SO-C-C.

tasks.title: Decision record
requirements: Maintain a dedicated blocker/decision queue with severity or urgency, concise explanation, affected milestone/tasks, dependencies, options, recommended next step, decision owner and the consequence of waiting.
Distinguish a genuine blocker requiring user action from an agent's internal retry, transient failure or routine subtask.
Keep routine retries, agent replacement, provider failover, lease expiry and execution recovery inside Memev. Do not turn ordinary infrastructure events into customer decisions.
Give each human decision a clear state: raised, awaiting user, answered, approved, rejected, deferred or resolved. Preserve the decision and its rationale in project history.
Let the lead agent explain the issue in plain language, present viable options and identify what it recommends and why. It must not present its recommendation as the user's decision.
When a decision is made, update the canonical project record and recalculate affected dependencies, plans, task eligibility and verification freshness.
Never silently skip permissions, invent an approval, discard a blocker or continue a consequential action that requires human authorisation.
